# Kael
> GPU-accelerated UI framework for native-first desktop apps in Rust. Aims to help builders ship high-performance native desktop apps without bundling Chromium, with WebView islands available when web compatibility is the right tool.
Kael renders via Metal (macOS), DirectX 11 (Windows), Vulkan (Linux). Apps are primarily Rust UI — no HTML/CSS/JS required for native surfaces. Use `webview(id, url)` for deliberate web-standard islands. One binary, native performance, 60fps (up to 120fps on ProMotion displays).

## Quick start

```toml
[dependencies]
kael = "0.3"
```

```rust
use kael::*;
use kael::prelude::*;

struct MyApp { count: i32 }

impl Render for MyApp {
    fn render(&mut self, _window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> impl IntoElement {
        let entity = cx.entity();
        div().size_full().flex().items_center().justify_center()
            .bg(rgb(0x1E1E1E)).text_color(rgb(0xFFFFFF))
            .child(format!("Count: {}", self.count))
            .child(button("inc").label("+1").on_click({
                let entity = entity.clone();
                move |_, _, cx| {
                    entity.update(cx, |this, cx| { this.count += 1; cx.notify(); });
                }
            }))
    }
}

fn main() {
    Application::new().run(|cx: &mut App| {
        let bounds = Bounds::centered(None, size(px(400.0), px(300.0)), cx);
        cx.open_window(
            WindowOptionsBuilder::new().title("My App").windowed(bounds),
            |_, cx| cx.new(|_| MyApp { count: 0 }),
        ).unwrap();
        cx.activate(true);
    });
}
```
## Architecture
- **Application::new().run(|cx| { ... })** — boots platform event loop
- **cx.open_window(options, |window, cx| cx.new(|_| View))** — creates a GPU window
- **Entity<T>** — reactive state container. Read with `.read(cx)`, mutate with `.update(cx, |this, cx| { ... })`
- **cx.notify()** — triggers re-render after state change
- **impl Render for T** — defines how an entity paints itself
- **div()** — base container element, Tailwind-style builder: `.flex()`, `.bg()`, `.text_color()`, `.child()`
- **impl Global for T** — app-wide singleton. Set with `cx.set_global()`, read with `cx.global::<T>()`
## Widget primitives
All widgets: `widget_name(id, value, ...)` → `.on_change(|value, window, cx| { ... })` → `.render_with(|state, ...| { ... })`
| Widget | Constructor | Key props |
|--------|-------------|-----------|
| button | `button(id)` | `.label()`, `.disabled()`, `.on_click()`, `.render_with(...)`; custom renderers should inspect `ButtonRenderState::to_text()`, `has_label()`, and `label_len_bytes()` without logging label text |
| text_input | `text_input(id, value)` | `.placeholder()`, `.multi_line()`, `.password()`, `.on_change()`, `.on_submit()`, `.render_with(|state, window, cx| ...)`; custom renderers should inspect `state.to_text()`, `value_len_bytes()`, `display_text_len_bytes()`, `placeholder_len_bytes()`, `has_placeholder()`, `is_masked_display()`, `line_count()`, `selection_rect_count()`, `has_selection()`, and `has_cursor()` without logging values/placeholders/selected text/coordinates |
| checkbox | `checkbox(id, checked)` | `.label()`, `.indeterminate()`, `.on_change()`, `.render_with(...)`; custom renderers should inspect `CheckboxRenderState::to_text()`, `has_label()`, and `label_len_bytes()` without logging label text |
| toggle | `toggle(id, on)` | `.label()`, `.on_change()`, `.render_with(...)`; custom renderers should inspect `ToggleRenderState::to_text()`, `has_label()`, and `label_len_bytes()` without logging label text |
| radio_group | `radio_group(id, value, options)` | `.on_change()`, `.disabled()`, `.render_with(...)`; custom renderers should inspect `RadioItemRenderState::to_text()`, `label_len_bytes()`, `is_first()`, and `is_last()` without logging option values or label text |
| slider | `slider(id, value)` | `.min()`, `.max()`, `.step()`, `.discrete()`, `.vertical()`, `.disabled()`, `.on_change()`, `.render_with(...)`; custom renderers should inspect `SliderRenderState::to_text()`, `position_class()`, `is_at_min()`, and `is_at_max()` without logging exact values/bounds/fractions |
| select | `select(id, value, options)` | `.placeholder()`, `.searchable()`, `.on_change()`, `.render_with(...)`, `.render_options_with(...)`, `.render_popup_with(...)`, `.render_search_with(...)`; custom renderers should inspect `SelectRenderState::to_text()`, `SelectOptionRenderState::to_text()`, `SelectPopupRenderState::to_text()`, and `SelectSearchRenderState::to_text()` plus byte/count helpers without logging display text, option labels, placeholders, search queries, option values, popup widths, or coordinates |
| date_picker | `date_picker(id, date)` | `.on_change()`, `.render_with(...)`, `.render_days_with(...)`, `.render_popup_with(...)`, `.render_header_with(...)`, `.render_nav_buttons_with(...)`, `.render_weekdays_with(...)`; custom renderers should inspect date picker render-state `to_text()` helpers for open/focus, label bytes, day selectable/selected/highlighted state, selected-highlighted relation, navigation availability, button direction/enabled state, and weekday index without logging exact dates, month names, weekday/button labels, popup widths, or coordinates |
| modal | `modal(id, open)` | `.label()`, `.backdrop()`, `.dismiss_on_escape()`, `.dismiss_on_click_outside()`, `.on_change()`, `.render_with(...)`; custom renderers should inspect `ModalRenderState::to_text()`, `has_label()`, `label_len_bytes()`, and `dismissal_mode()` without logging dialog labels |
| popover | `popover(id, open)` | `.render_anchor_with(...)`, `.render_popup_with(...)`, `.offset()`, `.dismiss_on_escape()`, `.dismiss_on_click_outside()`, `.on_open_change()`; custom renderers should inspect popover anchor/popup `to_text()` helpers plus `has_anchor_bounds()`, `width_class()`, and `dismissal_mode()` without logging exact widths/coordinates/bounds |
| menu_button | `menu_button(id, items)` | `.label()`, `.on_select()`, `.render_trigger_with(...)`, `.render_items_with(...)`; custom renderers should inspect menu trigger/item `to_text()` helpers plus `has_label()` and `label_len_bytes()` without logging trigger labels, item labels, or item values |
| tabs | `tabs(id, value, items)` | `.on_change()`, `.render_tabs_with(...)`; custom renderers should inspect `TabRenderState::to_text()`, `label_len_bytes()`, `is_first()`, and `is_last()` without logging tab values or label text |
| disclosure | `disclosure(id, open)` | `.label()`, `.panel()`, `.on_change()`, `.render_with(...)`; custom renderers should inspect `DisclosureRenderState::to_text()`, `has_label()`, and `label_len_bytes()` without logging trigger label text |
| progress | `progress(id, value)` | `.max()`, `.indeterminate()`, `.render_with(...)`; custom renderers should inspect `ProgressRenderState::to_text()`, `is_determinate()`, and `completion_class()` without logging exact values/max/fractions |
| toast | `Toast::new(title)` | `.body()`, `.duration()`, `.position()`; inspect `to_text()`, `has_body()`, `title_len_bytes()`, `body_len_bytes()`, `duration_class()`, and `position_key()` without logging title/body text or exact seconds |
| splitter | `splitter(id, px)` | `.min()`, `.max()`, `.step()`, `.discrete()`, `.horizontal()`, `.on_change()`, `.render_with(...)`; custom renderers should inspect `SplitterRenderState::to_text()`, `orientation()`, `position_class()`, `is_at_min()`, and `is_at_max()` without logging exact pixels/fractions |
| label | `label(id)` | `.text()`, `.for_focus_handle()`, child content; inspect `to_text()`, `has_text()`, `text_len_bytes()`, `has_target_focus()`, and `child_count()` without logging label text or child contents |
| scroll_bar | `scroll_bar(id, handle)` | `.horizontal()`, `.step()`, `.render_with(...)`; custom renderers should inspect `ScrollBarRenderState::to_text()`, `orientation()`, `has_overflow()`, `position_class()`, `thumb_size_class()`, `opacity_class()`, `is_at_start()`, and `is_at_end()` without logging exact offsets/sizes/ratios/coordinates |
| rich_text | `rich_text()` | `.text()`, `.styled(t, HighlightStyle)`, `.link()`, `.mention()`, `.hashtag()`, `.code()`, `.inline_element()`, `.selectable()`; inspect `to_text()`, `segment_count()`, `text_segment_count()`, `text_len_bytes()`, `inline_element_count()`, `entity_count()`, `link_count()`, `mention_count()`, `hashtag_count()`, `click_handler_count()`, `is_selectable()` without logging text, URLs, mentions, hashtags, code, or payloads |
| semantic | `menu_item(id)`, `link(id)`, `tree_item(id)` | `.label()`, `.url()`, `.selected()`, `.expanded()`, `.disabled()`, `.on_click()`; inspect `MenuEntry::to_text()`, `Link::to_text()`, `TreeItem::to_text()`, plus `AccessibilityRole/State/Action/Value/Attributes/Node/Tree::to_text()` and action/audit summaries for native DOM-like role/action/focus/hidden/value/audit readiness without logging labels, URLs, values, placeholders, descriptions, exact geometry, child contents, payload text, audit messages, or callbacks |
| navigator | `navigator(Route::new(id, view))` | prefer `cx.navigation_handoff_checked(NavigationHandoffBuilder::new().route(NavigationRouteDescriptorBuilder::new("home").restorable_state()).push_route("settings").restore_session(2).deep_link("myapp").hosted_history_bridge("docs"))?` before generated tabs, breadcrumbs, session restore, deep-link entry, or hosted-history fallback mutate navigation state; use `NavigationHandoff::to_text()`, `Route::to_text()`, `RouteChangeEvent::to_text()`, `Transition::to_text()`, and `Navigator::to_text()` for request kinds, next action, stack depth, route-id byte lengths, memento presence, current-route presence, and transition state without logging route IDs, URLs, tab labels, breadcrumbs, stored mementos, or views |
| uniform_list | `uniform_list(id, count, renderer)` | `.track_scroll()`, `.with_sizing_behavior()`, `.with_horizontal_sizing_behavior()`; inspect `UniformList::to_text()`, `UniformListScrollHandle::to_text()`, `ScrollStrategy::to_text()`, and shared list state/event summaries before generated large-list rendering or scroll-to-item flows without logging row contents, measured sizes, viewport pixels, or scroll offsets |
| recycling_list | `recycling_list(id, delegate)` | variable heights and element pooling; inspect `RecyclingList::to_text()` plus shared list state/event summaries for delegate item count, sizing, alignment, and coarse overdraw without logging row contents, measured heights, viewport pixels, exact overdraw, or scroll offsets |
| sortable_list | `sortable_list(id, delegate)` | `.with_sizing_behavior()`, `.with_alignment()`; use `sortable_reorder_plan(source, insertion, count).to_text()`, `has_move()`, `is_noop()`, `is_out_of_range()`, `target()`, `sortable_auto_scroll_class(...)`, list alignment/sizing `to_text()` keys, and shared list summaries around generated reorder flows without logging row contents, pointer coordinates, or geometry |
| canvas | `canvas(prepaint_fn, paint_fn)` | custom GPU drawing |
| cached | `cached(child)` | `.id()`; inspect `Cached::to_text()`, `has_child()`, and `has_explicit_id()` before generated expensive previews/subtrees without logging cache ids or child contents |
| deferred | `deferred(child)` | `.with_priority()`, `.priority()`; inspect `Deferred::to_text()`, `priority_value()`, and `priority_class()` for overlay paint ordering without logging child contents |
| effect_layer | `effect_layer(child)` | `.id()`, `.content_blur()`, `.drop_shadow()`; inspect `EffectLayer::to_text()`, effect/blur/shadow helpers, and explicit-id presence for compositor-style native effects without logging cache ids, child contents, blur radii, shadow offsets/colors, or geometry |
| layer_stack | `LayerStack::new()` with `LayerOptions::{modal,centered,fullscreen,anchored}` | inspect `LayerAnchor::to_text()`, `LayerOptions::to_text()`, and `LayerStack::to_text()` for placement, backdrop capture, priority class, dismissal policy, and layer counts without logging child views, colors, coordinates, margins, ids, or content |
| img | `img(source)` | `.object_fit()`, `.grayscale()`, `.with_loading()`, `.with_fallback()`; inspect `ImageSource::to_text()`, `ImageStyle::to_text()`, and `Img::to_text()` for source kind, resource byte length, object-fit key, loading/fallback hooks, and cache binding without logging URLs, file paths, asset names, bytes, image IDs, dimensions, or child contents |
| image_cache | `image_cache(lru(id, max))`, `image_cache(retain_all(id))` | choose retain-all for bounded asset sets and LRU for feeds/galleries/maps; inspect provider/cache/item/element `to_text()` helpers for policy, entry/loading/loaded/error counts, capacity class, at-capacity state, and child count without logging resource ids, element ids, image ids, bytes, error details, or asset names |
| svg | `svg()` | `.path()`, `.size()`, `.text_color()`, `.with_transformation()`; inspect `Svg::to_text()` and `Transformation::to_text()` for path presence/byte length and coarse transform kind without logging SVG paths, asset names, coordinates, scale values, or rotation values |
| surface | `surface(source)` | `.object_fit()`; inspect `SurfaceSource::to_text()` and `Surface::to_text()` for platform surface class and object-fit key without logging pixel contents or dimensions |
| lottie | `lottie(source)` | `.autoplay()`, `.loop_forever()`, `.ping_pong()` |
## Desktop-gap guidance
- Prefer native Kael UI for app chrome, dashboards, tools, editors, panes, and controls; for capability audits, classify the app type first (media, file/project explorer, dashboard, developer tool, collaboration, creative/canvas, commerce, or plugin-heavy app), start with `DesktopCapabilityPortfolioAudit::all(&CapabilityReport::current())` plus `DesktopSurfaceAuditPlan::all(&CapabilityReport::current())` / `DesktopSurfaceArea::all()` for broad framework audits, then inspect `audit.action_items()`, `audit.blocking_action_items()`, - Use `matrix.native_first_plan()` when native desktop capability work includes both native gaps and WebView islands; inspect `phases()`, `current_phase()`, `current_phase_assignment()`, `current_execution_kit()`, `current_execution_batch()`, `current_ticket()`, `current_generation_pass()`, `can_generate_native_now()`, and `should_defer_webview()` so blockers, native primitive generation, and evidence happen before browser compatibility islands; use phase `assignment()`, `execution_kits()`, `execution_batch()`, and `evidence_checklists()` for scheduler counts, concrete starter payloads, serializable batches, and proof work; call `native_first.continue_with_execution_batch_evidence(&batch, checklists)`, `matrix.ready_readiness_decision()` / `native_first.ready_readiness_decision()`, or `matrix.readiness_decision(checklists)` / `native_first.readiness_decision(checklists)` before stating readiness.
- Prefer `let handoff = cx.embedded_hosted_view_handoff_checked(EmbeddedHostedViewHandoffBuilder::new().native_pane("main-pane").cached_deferred_pane("preview").floating_pane("inspector").hosted_pane("oauth", EmbeddedHostedPaneProfile::AuthFlow).controller_ownership("oauth").support_preflight().roadmap_work(reason))?; tracing::info!(summary = handoff.to_text(), next = ?handoff.next_action(), "embedded hosted view handoff")` before generated apps open embedded panes, then inspect `EmbeddedHostedViewNextAction` so agents compose native panes, bound expensive panes, place floating panes, create explicit hosted panes, attach pane-scoped controllers, preflight support, or track roadmap work without logging pane ids, route ids, tab labels, URLs, storage keys, selectors, document text, view contents, focus ids, bounds, hosted payloads, or roadmap text. Use `webview(id, url)` plus `webview_controller(id)` for small embeds; use `webview_file(id, path)?` / `webview_file_with_options(id, path, options)?` for desktop-app local `loadFile` islands, and `webview_html(id, html)` / `webview_html_with_options(id, html, options)` for true inline `loadHTML` islands; prefer `webview_with_options(id, url, WebViewOptions::auth_flow(storage_key))` for OAuth/SSO/account pages, `WebViewOptions::embedded_widget()` for payments/maps/docs/customer widgets, and `WebViewOptions::web_graphics()` for browser-only WebGL/WebGPU/canvas islands; add `.devtools()` while developing WebView islands; use `.on_console_message(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.console_bridge(kind)` when native diagnostics, tests, or agents should receive hosted-page console output and uncaught errors; use `.zoom_hotkeys()` or `.zoom_hotkeys_enabled(true)` when browser content should own zoom shortcuts/gestures; use `.on_keyboard_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.keyboard_event_bridge(kind)` when native chrome should observe hosted keydown, keyup, and beforeinput activity for shortcut coordination or tests; use `.on_location_changed(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.location_bridge(kind)` when native tabs, breadcrumbs, Back/Forward chrome, or agents should observe hosted SPA route changes; use `.on_lifecycle_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.lifecycle_bridge(kind)` when native chrome, resource throttling, tests, or agents should observe hosted focus, visibility, page show/hide, and browser fullscreen changes; use `.on_scroll_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.scroll_bridge(kind)` when native progress, sticky chrome, scroll restoration, tests, or agents should observe hosted scroll and viewport state; use `.on_selection_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.selection_bridge(kind)` when native edit menus, formatting chrome, tests, or agents should observe hosted selection state; use `.media_autoplay()` or `.media_autoplay_enabled(...)` for browser-media islands that need explicit autoplay policy; use `.on_media_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` when native chrome should receive browser audio/video play, pause, seek, time, volume, rate, buffering, metadata, and error events; use `.on_context_menu(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` when native chrome should own right-click or secondary-click menus for hosted WebView content with selected text, link, image, media, editable, and input context; use `.on_pointer_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.pointer_bridge(kind)` when native status bars, hover previews, click handling, tests, or agents need lightweight link/image/media/editable context for hosted content; use `.on_form_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.form_bridge(kind)` when native validation, progress chrome, tests, or agents should observe hosted submit, reset, change, and input activity without bespoke page JavaScript; use `.on_file_input_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.file_input_bridge(kind)` when native upload chrome, tests, or agents should observe browser file-input selections with file names, sizes, MIME types, and last-modified timestamps; use `.on_resource_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.resource_bridge(kind)` when native diagnostics, loading UI, tests, or agents should observe hosted subresource timing plus element load/error activity without request interception; use `.on_network_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.network_bridge(kind)` when native diagnostics, loading UI, tests, or agents should observe hosted fetch/XHR outcomes without opening devtools; use `.on_dialog_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.dialog_bridge(kind)` when native diagnostics, tests, or agents should observe hosted alert, confirm, prompt, and beforeunload activity while preserving browser behavior; use `.on_clipboard_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.clipboard_event_bridge(kind)` when native editor chrome, tests, or agents should observe hosted copy/cut/paste events and browser-exposed clipboard data; use `.on_permission_request(kind, |request, window, cx| ...)` or `.permission_bridge(kind)` when native app policy should preflight hosted camera, microphone, display-capture, geolocation, or notification requests before browser prompts continue; use `.on_storage_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.storage_bridge(kind)` when native account chrome, settings sync, tests, or agents should observe hosted localStorage/sessionStorage changes without polling JavaScript; use controller `select_media_text_track(window, selector)` and `disable_media_text_tracks(window)` for browser text tracks; use controller `request_media_fullscreen(window)`, `exit_media_fullscreen(window)`, `request_media_picture_in_picture(window)`, and `exit_media_picture_in_picture(window)` for WebView-hosted video fullscreen/PiP requests subject to browser support and user-gesture policy; use `.background_color(color)` or `.transparent_background()` when an embed should inherit native chrome instead of showing the default WebView rectangle; use `.focused()` or `.focused_enabled(...)` when auth, checkout, editor, or browser-widget islands should take keyboard focus immediately on Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend; use `.clipboard_access()` or `.clipboard_access_enabled(...)` when hosted rich editors, docs widgets, or browser pages need JavaScript clipboard APIs; use `.javascript_disabled()` or `.javascript_disabled_enabled(...)` for untrusted static docs or previews that should not run page scripts; use `.general_autofill_enabled(false)` or `.general_autofill_disabled()` for Windows/WebView2 general form suggestions, and choose popup behavior with `.deny_new_windows()`, `.open_new_windows_in_current_webview()`, `.allow_new_windows()`, or `.on_new_window(...)` returning `WebViewNewWindowPolicy::{Deny, NavigateCurrent, Allow}`; Linux/Windows honor all policies, while Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend honors `Deny`, `NavigateCurrent`, and `Allow` for target-blank requests; macOS `Allow` creates a WebKit-managed popup child WebView inside the same native window, so prefer `NavigateCurrent` or a custom handler when app-owned route/chrome/lifecycle matters; choose download behavior with `.allow_downloads()`, `.deny_downloads()`, `.on_download_started(...)` returning `WebViewDownloadPolicy::{Allow, Deny, SaveTo(path)}`, and `.on_download_completed(...)` for completion handoff; use controller `trigger_download(window, url, filename, callback)` or `download_url(window, url, filename, callback)` for native Save link/image/media commands based on context-menu or pointer bridge URLs; use `.on_document_title_changed(...)` to sync hosted page titles into native window titles, tabs, breadcrumbs, or labels; use `.on_favicon_changed(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.favicon_bridge(kind)` when hosted pages should drive native tab icons, breadcrumbs, history rows, or app switchers; use `.on_page_load(...)` with `WebViewPageLoadEvent::{Started, Finished}` for loading spinners, ready coordination, and auth-flow progress; use `.on_location_changed(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` for event-driven hosted SPA URL/title/readyState and Back/Forward chrome sync, and `.on_lifecycle_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` for hosted focus/visibility/pagehide/pageshow/fullscreen sync, and `.on_scroll_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` for hosted scroll/viewport progress sync, and `.on_selection_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` for hosted selected text/HTML sync on Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend; use `.on_drag_drop(...)` returning `WebViewDragDropPolicy::{AllowBrowserDefault, BlockBrowserDefault}` or `.block_drag_drop()` when hosted content can receive local file drops and the app must preserve or block browser defaults explicitly. Refine options with `.storage_key(...)`, `.html(...)`, `.clear_html(...)`, `.user_agent(...)`, `.inject_css(...)`, `.inject_javascript(...)`, `.bridge_script()`, `.console_bridge(kind)`, `stop_loading(window)`, `play_media(window)`, `pause_media(window)`, `set_media_muted(window, muted)`, `set_media_volume(window, volume)`, `set_media_playback_rate(window, rate)`, callback)`, `selected_text(window, callback)`, `selected_html(window, callback)`, `document_html(window, callback)`, `document_snapshot(window, callback)`, `element_snapshot(window, selector, callback)`, `capture_dom_image(window, selector, WebViewDomImageCaptureOptions::default(), callback)`, `trigger_download(window, url, filename, callback)`, `download_url(window, url, filename, callback)`, `favicons(window, callback)`, `edit_command(window, WebViewEditCommand::Copy, callback)`, `print(window)`, `clear_browsing_data(window)`, `storage_snapshot(window, callback)`, `set_storage_item(window, WebViewStorageArea::Local, key, value, callback)`, `remove_storage_item(window, WebViewStorageArea::Session, key, callback)`, and `clear_storage_area(window, area, callback)` instead of repeating raw ids. Use `element_snapshot(window, selector, callback)` to inspect one top-document hosted element before acting; it returns `Result<Option<WebViewElementSnapshot>, SharedString>` with tag, id, classes, normalized text, form state, link/src context, viewport rect, attributes, and computed display/visibility/pointer-events, and returns `Ok(None)` for no match. Use selector DOM customization helpers for app-owned hosted widgets, third-party embeds with stable selectors, visual test setup, and AI-agent customization without raw JavaScript; they return `Result<bool, SharedString>` and do not pierce cross-origin frames or shadow roots. Use `storage_snapshot(...)` plus storage mutation helpers for hosted auth/session debugging, carts, draft seeding, tests, and agent state inspection; callbacks report readable entries or browser storage errors, and origin/sandbox/quota rules still apply. Use `capture_dom_image(...)` for same-document SVG data URL previews of app-owned widgets, receipts, and agent visual artifacts; it is not a native pixel screenshot or full hosted page capture equivalent, and it does not serialize cross-origin frames, shadow roots, video/canvas/WebGL pixels, or all external resources faithfully. `print(window)` opens the native print dialog on Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend. Treat WebView devtools as a debug/development aid: Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews can open, close, and report `is_devtools_open(window, callback)` state in debug/devtools builds; Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend honors `.devtools()` by marking the view inspectable for Safari/Web Inspector, but WKWebView does not expose public APIs to programmatically open, close, or report inspector window state. Treat WebView downloads as supported on Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend; macOS `Allow` resolves to `~/Downloads` with WebKit's suggested filename, while `SaveTo(path)` must still be absolute; `trigger_download(...)` dispatches a browser `<a download>` action and returns `WebViewDownloadTriggerResult`, but browser policy, origin rules, response headers, and download handlers still decide the final destination and success. Treat WebView drag/drop hooks as supported on Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend; macOS forwards to WebKit when handlers return `AllowBrowserDefault` and blocks WebKit default handling when they return `BlockBrowserDefault`. Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend honor `.on_document_title_changed(...)`. Use `.request_headers(headers)` on `WebViewOptions` for initial loads and `navigate_with_headers(window, url, headers)` for later navigations with `http_client::http::HeaderMap`, matching hosted main-frame header injection style main-frame request headers on Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend; subresource requests stay controlled by the embedded browser engine. Use `url(window, callback)` for desktop-app `hosted page controller.getURL()`; Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews return the backend current URL, and Kael's custom macOS WebView backend reads `WKWebView.URL.absoluteString` with a declared-URL fallback before a page has committed. Use `evaluate_javascript_with_result(window, script, callback)` for desktop-app `executeJavaScript` value returns; Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend deliver JSON string serialization through `Result<SharedString, SharedString>`. Use `cookies(window, callback)` or `cookies_for_url(window, url, callback)` for Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend session inspection; callbacks receive `Result<Vec<WebViewCookie>, SharedString>` with name, value, domain, path, secure, and http-only metadata. Use `set_cookie(window, WebViewCookie::new(name, value).domain(domain).path(path), callback)` and `delete_cookie(window, cookie, callback)` for session mutation; mutation callbacks receive `Result<(), SharedString>`. Use `clear_browsing_data(window)` for logout, account switching, demo reset, and test isolation; Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WebView backend clear browser storage through their profile data stores; persistent `.storage_key(...)` / `WebViewOptions::auth_flow(...)` profiles are the cleanup boundary. General autofill control is currently a Windows/WebView2-only option and does not disable password or credit-card autofill. Browser zoom hotkeys/gestures are currently Windows/WebView2-backed; Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend handles standard Command-plus, Command-minus, Command-zero, and trackpad magnification zoom through WKWebView pageZoom; use controller `set_zoom_factor(window, factor)` for native app-owned zoom on Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend. Treat JavaScript clipboard access as a Wry-backed construction option on Linux/Windows; Kael's custom macOS WebView backend injects an opt-in native text bridge for `navigator.clipboard.readText()`, `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)`, the `text/plain` subset of `navigator.clipboard.read()`/`write(...)`, and legacy `document.execCommand("copy")`/`"cut"` text selection calls backed by NSPasteboard, while broader clipboard item MIME types remain controlled by WebKit and macOS permissions; Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend honor `.media_autoplay(...)`, `.media_autoplay_enabled(...)`, `.background_color(...)`, `.transparent_background()`, `.javascript_disabled()`, and `.javascript_disabled_enabled(...)`; WKWebView clipboard behavior is controlled by macOS, page permissions, and app menu accelerators. Do not combine `.javascript_disabled()` with `.bridge_script()`, `.inject_javascript(...)`, or hosted widgets that require page JavaScript. `WebViewDownloadPolicy::SaveTo(path)` must use an absolute path. For pages you control, inject `.bridge_script()` and call `window.kael.post(kind, payload, id)` for fire-and-forget or `await window.kael.invoke(kind, payload, { timeoutMs })` for request/response. Rust receives `WebViewBridgeMessage { kind, id, payload }` and should reply with the controller helpers.
- Native media exists as primitives (`MediaSource`, `audio(source)`, `video(source)`) plus `VideoController` for metadata, play/pause/stop/seek/fast-seek, source replacement, volume/mute, loop, audio playback-rate control through `AudioHandle::set_speed`, `VideoSnapshot::ready_state`, `VideoSnapshot::buffered_ranges`, WebVTT/SRT text tracks, and `VideoEvent`s including `SourceChanged`, `Progress`, `ReadyStateChange`, `CanPlay`, `CanPlayThrough`, and `Waiting`. Prefer `let handoff = cx.video_element_handoff_checked(VideoElementHandoffBuilder::url(url).initial_controls(VideoPlaybackControlsBuilder::new().volume(v).playback_rate(rate)).playlist(VideoPlaylist::new([MediaSource::url(url)])))?; tracing::info!(summary = handoff.to_text(), "video element handoff"); let instruction = handoff.render_instruction(); let media_keys = handoff.media_key_binding_builder_checked()?; let customization = cx.video_element_customization_plan_checked(VideoElementCustomizationPlanBuilder::new(handoff.clone()).html_video_baseline().timeline_scrubbing().captions_ui().fullscreen().picture_in_picture().playlist_media_keys())?` for generated desktop-app URL players that need source routing, initial controls, playlist/media-key intent, requirement coverage, Electron-style custom properties/events/controls/presentation checks, and native-vs-WebView next actions in one object; use `VideoUrlPlaybackHandoff::url(url)?` for the smaller source-to-render handoff; use `let builder = VideoPlaybackPlanBuilder::url(url).content_type(content_type).webview_options(WebViewVideoOptions::default().checked()?); tracing::info!(summary = builder.to_text(), "video playback plan builder"); let plan = builder.build_checked()?; tracing::info!(summary = plan.to_text(), "video playback plan")` for generated desktop-app URL video players: it validates the source, MIME/content type, WebView fallback options, returns `VideoPlaybackPlanTarget::{Native, WebViewFallback}`, exposes `render_instruction()` as `VideoPlaybackRenderInstruction::{Native { controller }, WebViewFallback { page_url, element_id, reason }}` plus `render_instruction().to_text()`, `can_play()`, `route()`, `controller()`, `webview_page_url()`, and `webview_element_id()`, routes HLS/DASH manifests or adaptive MIME types to browser-video fallback, and rejects memory-backed sources when WebView fallback is requested; use `handoff.requirement_plan()`, `handoff.next_action()`, `handoff.is_ready()`, `handoff.controller_checked()`, `handoff.media_key_binding_builder_checked()`, `VideoElementCustomizationPlanBuilder`, `VideoElementCustomizationFeature`, `VideoElementCustomizationNextAction`, or `VideoUrlPlaybackHandoff::{baseline_requirement_plan,full_requirement_plan,baseline_next_action,baseline_ready}`, `VideoPlaybackRequirement::url_player_baseline()`, `VideoPlaybackRequirement::all()`, `plan.requirement_plan([VideoPlaybackRequirement::BasicPlayback, VideoPlaybackRequirement::TextTracks, VideoPlaybackRequirement::AdaptiveStreaming, VideoPlaybackRequirement::HardwareDecode])` or `builder.build_requirement_plan_checked([...])` before rendering generated players that require adaptive streaming, PiP, fast seek, playback rate, hardware decode, native stream selection, or custom video-element chrome; inspect `satisfied_count()`, `limited_count()`, `missing_count()`, `missing_requirements()`, `next_action()`, `requires_webview_fallback()`, `webview_fallback_requirements()`, `requires_native_backend_work()`, `native_backend_work_requirements()`, and `to_text()` to decide whether to render the planned route, accept limited support, use WebView fallback, configure playlist/handlers, or queue native backend work without logging media URLs, paths, MIME strings, generated data URLs, fallback reasons, caption text, exact seek/volume/rate values, or exact gap labels. Use `MediaSourceBuilder::file(path).require_existing_file().canonicalize_file().build_checked()?` for local video files, `MediaSourceBuilder::bytes(bytes)` / `.reader(key, open)` for non-URL sources, `MediaSourceBuilder::to_text()` for content-safe source-kind/file-check summaries, and raw `MediaSource::{url,file,bytes,reader}` for custom FFmpeg inputs. Query `video_capability_report().to_text()` plus `full_count()`, `partial_count()`, `roadmap_count()`, `native_gap_count()`, `has_native_gaps()`, and `has_webview_fallback()` for the honest `VideoCapabilityStatus::{Full, Partial, Roadmap}` matrix; hardware decode, native adaptive streaming, and native stream selection are Roadmap. Pitch-preserving time stretching is not implemented yet. Use `can_play_video_type(...)`, `can_play_video_source(...)`, or `VideoController::can_play_source()` for browser-style `VideoCanPlay::{No, Maybe, Probably}` confidence; use `recommended_video_playback_route(&source)`, `recommended_video_playback_route_for_type(content_type)`, or `VideoController::recommended_route()` before advanced media UI: direct files/URLs default to native playback, while HLS `.m3u8`, DASH `.mpd`, and adaptive streaming MIME types such as `application/vnd.apple.mpegurl` or `application/dash+xml` return `VideoPlaybackRoute::WebViewRecommended` until native streaming backends land; use the MIME helper for extensionless CDN URLs. For URL/file sources that need WebView fallback, call `webview_video_player_url(&source, &WebViewVideoOptions::default().checked()?)` and pass the returned data URL to `webview(id, page_url)`. `WebViewVideoOptions` supports browser-video controls/autoplay/muted/loop/playsinline/object-fit plus poster, preload (`WebViewVideoPreload`), crossorigin (`WebViewVideoCrossOrigin`), controlslist, disablePictureInPicture, initial start time, and WebVTT `<track>` tags through `WebViewVideoTextTrack` or `.webvtt_text_track(...)`; `.validate()` / `.checked()` rejects invalid poster/track URLs, controls-list tokens, text-track metadata, and unsafe object-fit values before embedding browser media, while `.to_text()` summarizes booleans/counts without logging poster URLs, track URLs, or caption text. Use `VideoController::dispatch_webview_command_checked(window, WebViewVideoCommandBuilder::...)` to drive the browser fallback from an existing controller with validated play/pause/toggle/stop, exact/fast seek, volume, mute, playback rate, loop, text-track selection/disablement, browser fullscreen, picture-in-picture, and snapshot requests; use `WebViewVideoCommandBuilder::to_text()` / `command_kind()` before dispatch so traces report command kind and seek/audio/presentation classes without exact seek positions, volume/rate values, or text-track selectors; the checked path rejects invalid generated volumes, rates, seek targets, and text-track selectors before running WebView JavaScript, while raw `dispatch_webview_command(window, WebViewVideoCommand::...)` remains available for hand-validated integrations. The fallback posts `kael-video-event` updates for playback plus selected text tracks, active cues, browser fullscreen, and picture-in-picture so `VideoPlayer` callbacks and `on_event(...)` can stay in sync with browser state. Lower-level helpers `webview_video_player_id(&source)` and `webview_video_player_command_script(WebViewVideoCommand::...)` are available when manually calling `Window::evaluate_webview_javascript(...)`. Use `VideoController::url(...)`, `.file(...)`, `.bytes(...)`, `.reader(...)`, or `.new(MediaSource::...)` for custom media control; replace media at runtime with `.set_source_checked(MediaSourceBuilder::...)`, `.set_url_checked(...)`, `.set_file_checked(...)`, `.set_bytes_checked(...)`, or `.set_reader_checked(...)` so invalid generated sources fail before controller mutation, then reset media-derived state while preserving volume/mute/rate/loop/text-track configuration; raw `.set_source(...)`, `.set_url(...)`, `.set_file(...)`, `.set_bytes(...)`, and `.set_reader(...)` remain available for hand-validated integrations. Use `VideoPlaylist::new([MediaSource::url(...), ...]).repeat(true)` with `MediaKeyBindingBuilder::playlist(...)` for simple next/previous source replacement on hardware media keys. The controller also supports fluent setup with `.preload_metadata()`, `.volume(...)`, `.muted(...)`, `.playback_rate(...)`, `.looping(...)`, `.start_at(...)`, `.srt_text_track(...)`, `.webvtt_text_track(...)`, `.text_track(...)`, `.selected_text_track(...)`, and `.text_track_disabled()`. Prefer `controller.add_text_track_checked(TextTrackBuilder::...)`, `.add_srt_text_track_checked(...)`, and `.add_webvtt_text_track_checked(...)` for generated caption/subtitle setup so empty metadata, empty parsed cue sets, invalid cue ranges, and duplicate track ids fail before controller state changes. Prefer `controller.select_text_track_checked(id)` and `controller.disable_text_track_checked()` for generated caption/subtitle controls so malformed ids, unknown tracks, and double-disable actions fail without silently changing active cues; raw `.text_track(...)`, `.srt_text_track(...)`, `.webvtt_text_track(...)`, `.select_text_track(...)`, and `.disable_text_track()` remain available for permissive app-owned flows. Prefer `controller.apply_controls_checked(VideoPlaybackControlsBuilder::new().volume(v).muted(m).playback_rate(rate).looping(looping).fast_seek_secs(seconds))?` plus `controls.to_text()` for generated player controls so empty updates, NaN/infinite values, volume outside `0.0..=1.0`, rates outside `0.0625..=16.0`, negative seek seconds, and extremely large seek positions fail before controller mutation and traces avoid exact seek/volume/rate values; raw setters remain available for hand-validated integrations. Read simple state with `.playback_state()`, `.current_time()` / `.current_time_secs()`, `.set_current_time(...)`, `.set_current_time_secs(...)`, `.fast_seek(...)`, `.fast_seek_secs(...)`, or `.set_position(...)`, `.duration()` / `.duration_secs()`, `.metadata()`, `.ready_state()`, `.buffered_ranges()`, `.volume_level()`, `.is_muted()` / `.muted_state()`, `.playback_rate_value()` / `.rate()`, `.is_looping()` / `.looping_enabled()`, `.text_tracks()`, `.active_text_track()`, `.selected_text_track_id()`, and `.error()`; use `.snapshot()` for aggregate state and time/cue/end event emission. Use `kael_ui::VideoPlayer::url(url, cx)` for the easiest URL-driven player; it defaults to `VideoPlayerRoute::Auto`, which renders normal URL/file media natively and automatically routes HLS/DASH browser-media manifests to a WebView-hosted `<video controls>` fallback that posts browser media events back into `VideoPlayer` callbacks and `.on_event(...)`. Call `.content_type(content_type)` on `VideoPlayer` when Auto should route an extensionless URL from a `Content-Type` header. Use `.native_playback()` to force native rendering, `.webview_fallback()` to force the browser video fallback for URL/file sources, or `.webview_options(WebViewVideoOptions::default().checked()?)` to tune the fallback page. `VideoPlayer::file(...)`, `VideoPlayer::bytes(...)`, `VideoPlayer::reader(...)`, and `VideoPlayer::source(MediaSource::...)` cover other source types. The wrapper renders active text-track cues, exposes loaded caption/subtitle tracks through its built-in controls, uses `fast_seek(...)` while scrubbing the timeline, toggles real platform fullscreen through `Window::toggle_fullscreen()` for the fullscreen button/`f` key, routes keyboard and chrome interactions through the same play/seek/volume/fullscreen callbacks, and supports attribute-style configuration with `.object_fit(...)`, `.playback_route(VideoPlayerRoute::Auto)`, `.content_type(...)`, `.preload(VideoPreload::Metadata)`, `.controls(...)`, `.autoplay()`, `.volume(...)`, `.muted(...)`, `.playback_rate(...)`, `.looping(...)`, `.start_at(...)`, `.show_captions(...)`, `.caption_style(...)`, `.srt_text_track(...)`, `.webvtt_text_track(...)`, `.text_track(...)`, `.select_text_track(...)`, and `.disable_text_track()`. Use `.on_source_changed(...)`, `.on_loaded_metadata(...)`, `.on_ready_state_change(...)`, `.on_can_play(...)`, `.on_can_play_through(...)`, `.on_waiting(...)`, `.on_progress(...)`, `.on_playing(...)`, `.on_paused(...)`, `.on_stopped(...)`, `.on_time_update(...)`, `.on_seeked(...)`, `.on_volume_changed(...)`, `.on_rate_change(...)`, `.on_loop_change(...)`, `.on_text_track_added(...)`, `.on_text_track_changed(...)`, `.on_cue_change(...)`, `.on_ended(...)`, and `.on_error(...)` for common video events; use `.on_event(...)` for the full event stream. Use `VideoPlayer::new(state)` for custom controls/state integrations.
- Inspect `VideoPlayer::to_text()`, `VideoPlayerState::to_text()`, `VideoCaptionStyle::to_text()`, `AudioPlayer::to_text()`, `AudioPlayerState::to_text()`, and `Waveform::to_text()` for source kind, route, player size, controls/captions/poster/source/title presence, progress/volume buckets, handler counts, waveform sample counts, and media-widget wiring without logging media URLs, file paths, titles, caption text, exact seek times, volume/rate values, waveform amplitudes, or colors; for Web Audio-style apps prefer `let audio = cx.audio_workflow_handoff_checked(AudioWorkflowHandoffBuilder::new().playback_source(AudioPlaybackSourceBuilder::url(url)).permission_preflight(AudioPermissionPreflightBuilder::new().microphone().system_audio()).privacy_manifest(AppPrivacyManifestBuilder::new().permission(AppPrivacyPermissionBuilder::microphone(reason)).permission(AppPrivacyPermissionBuilder::screen_capture(reason))).recording_capture(CaptureConfigSetBuilder::new().microphone().system_audio()).waveform_evidence(1, 2048))?` before generated soundboards recorders timeline audio waveform tools or system-audio capture claim native readiness; inspect `AudioWorkflowNextAction` and `audio.to_text()` without logging media URLs file paths reader keys byte payloads device filters permission reasons waveform samples capability notes or roadmap text; keep arbitrary AudioContext graphs AudioWorklet processors offline rendering sample-accurate scheduling and imported DAW widgets as explicit hosted audio islands or roadmap work until native graph APIs land.
- For native layout/CSS/canvas/SVG/WebGL parity, move down the native-first graphics ladder: `cx.layout_styling_handoff_checked(LayoutStylingHandoffBuilder::new().theme_tokens("main").responsive_layout("shell").transition_motion("routes").layer_effect("overlays").virtualized_list("rows").headless_render_evidence("shell", 2).hosted_css_island("legacy").roadmap_work(reason))?` plus `LayoutStylingNextAction` for generated style-system routing; plan CSS media-query replacement with `cx.responsive_layout_plan_checked(ResponsiveLayoutPlanBuilder::new("shell").breakpoint("xs", 0, ResponsiveLayoutMode::Stack, 1).breakpoint("lg", 1024, ResponsiveLayoutMode::Split, 3).splitter_policy().restore_focus().evidence_snapshots(2))?`, map imported CSS design systems with `cx.css_token_migration_checked(CssTokenMigrationBuilder::new().map("--color-primary", "primary").map("--space-md", "space_md").dark_mode().require_all_referenced_tokens())?`, and model CSS keyframes/Web Animations with `cx.animation_timeline_checked(AnimationTimelineBuilder::new().step("enter", Duration::from_millis(180)).easing_last(Easing::EaseOutCubic).keyframes_last(3).reduce_motion_fallback())?` before scheduling native motion. Then prefer `kael_ui` component -> styled `div()` -> headless controller -> canvas/path/image/SVG/Lottie -> WebView -> custom render target/shader roadmap; `to_text()` avoids surface ids, breakpoint ids, token names/values, CSS, keyframe ids, geometry, content, and roadmap text. Use `let graphics = graphics_capability_report(); tracing::info!(summary = graphics.to_text(), "graphics capabilities")` before promising desktop-app graphics readiness: native styled elements/canvas/paths/gradients/SVG/Lottie are `Full`, clip shapes/effect layers/headless rendering are `Partial`, browser-only graphics are `WebView`, and public render targets/custom shaders are `Roadmap`; use `count_status(...)`, `has_webview_fallbacks()`, and `has_roadmap_gaps()` to classify requirements.
- For performance claims, first prefer `cx.performance_evidence_handoff_checked(PerformanceEvidenceHandoffBuilder::new().process_metrics().resource_budget(AppResourceBudgetBuilder::new()...).benchmark_scenario(scenario).benchmark_sample_pair(pair).baseline_comparison(report))?` and inspect `PerformanceEvidenceNextAction`; raw evidence still comes from `cx.runtime_snapshot_checked(AppRuntimeSnapshotQueryBuilder::new())`, `cx.current_process_metrics()`, `cx.evaluate_resource_budget_checked(...)`, comparable `BenchmarkSamplePair` values built with `BenchmarkSampleApp::builder(BenchmarkSampleRuntime::{Baseline, Kael}, scenario, name)` and required interactions from `BenchmarkScenario::workload_spec()`, then `BaselineComparisonReport::generate_with_sample_pairs(...)`; do not state memory/CPU/startup wins while `report.evidence_issues` is non-empty (`MissingResult`, `DuplicateResult`, `EnvironmentMismatch`, `MissingSample`, and missing metrics all block claims).
## Component library (kael_ui)
Add `kael_ui = "0.3"` for 100+ shadcn-inspired components — no external component library needed. Before generated app chrome is rendered, prefer `let handoff = cx.app_chrome_surface_handoff_checked(AppChromeSurfaceHandoffBuilder::new().initialize_native_ui().app_shell("main-shell").data_surface("project-grid").command_palette("commands").accessibility_audit("main-a11y").hosted_web_ui("legacy-widget").roadmap_work(reason))?; tracing::info!(summary = handoff.to_text(), next = ?handoff.next_action(), "app chrome surface handoff")` and inspect `AppChromeSurfaceNextAction` so agents initialize native UI, build shell/data surfaces, register command palettes, audit accessibility, route hosted web UI, or track roadmap work without logging surface ids, labels, row data, document text, command labels, theme tokens, hosted ids, roadmap text, or generated view contents. Import everything with a single `use kael_ui::prelude::*;` (do not also glob-import `kael::*`; the prelude re-exports the essentials). Initialize with `kael_ui::init(cx)` then `install_theme(cx, Theme::dark())` — 18 presets, or brand your app with `Theme::custom(ThemeTokens { primary, ..ThemeTokens::dark() })`; re-installing a theme restyles all open windows live.
- **components** — Button, Input, Select, Combobox, Checkbox, Radio, Slider, DatePicker, TimePicker, ColorPicker, OtpInput, FileUpload, TagInput, Rating, Calendar, Carousel, code Editor (tree-sitter), and more; inspect `Position::to_text()`, `Selection::to_text()`, `FoldRange::to_text()`, `EditorDiagnostic::to_text()`, `EditorState::to_text()`, and `Editor::to_text()` for language/line/content-byte/cursor/selection/modified/file-presence/undo/redo/syntax/search/fold/readonly/diagnostic/customization coverage without logging document text, file paths, selected text, search terms, diagnostic messages, or callbacks
- **display** — Table, DataTable, DataGrid, Card, Badge, Accordion, Markdown/HTML rendering; inspect `ColumnDef::to_text()`, `DataTableState::to_text()`, `DataTable::to_text()`, `RowAction::to_text()`, `GridColumnDef::to_text()`, `DataGridState::to_text()`, and `DataGrid::to_text()` for column/row/virtual/cache/page/sort/selection/search/edit/action/load-more/fetch wiring without logging column ids, headers, row values, action labels, edit text, queries, dimensions, coordinates, or callbacks
- **navigation** — Sidebar, Menu, Tabs, Breadcrumbs, Toolbar, FileTree, StatusBar; inspect `MenuItem::to_text()`, `Menu::to_text()`, `ContextMenu::to_text()`, and `MenuBar::to_text()` for item/nesting/action/disabled/submenu/separator/shortcut coverage without logging ids, labels, shortcuts, coordinates, or callbacks
- **overlays** — Dialog, Sheet, BottomSheet, Popover, Toast, Tooltip, ContextMenu, CommandPalette; inspect `Dialog::to_text()`, `DialogHeader::to_text()`, `DialogPosition::to_text()`, `Sheet::to_text()`, `BottomSheet::to_text()`, `Command::to_text()`, and `CommandPaletteState::to_text()` for size/purpose/dismissal/header/content/footer/query/selection/recent/category/shortcut/executable coverage without logging ids, labels, titles, descriptions, categories, dimensions, coordinates, shortcut strings, child contents, queries, or callbacks
- **charts** — line, area, bar, pie, donut, radar, gauge, heatmap, treemap, sparkline
- **layout** — VStack, HStack, Grid, ScrollContainer, responsive breakpoints
- **theme** — shadcn-style design tokens, light/dark; `Theme` is a `Global`, read it in render with `Theme::of(cx).tokens.*` (`use_theme()` is the legacy clone-per-call shim)
- Bundled: 1,600+ Lucide icons (`set_icon_base_path("assets/icons")`), Inter + JetBrains Mono fonts
