## Animations

Bring `AnimationExt` into scope, then `element.with_animation(id, animation, |el, delta| el.mutate(delta))` where `delta` is eased progress `0.0..=1.0`.
`Animation::new(Duration)` `.with_easing(fn)` `.easing(Easing)` `.delay(d)` `.repeat(Repeat)` `.repeat_forever()`
`Easing`: `Linear` `EaseIn` `EaseOut` `EaseInOut` `CubicBezier(x1,y1,x2,y2)` `Spring{stiffness,damping,mass}` `Custom(Rc<Fn>)`. `Repeat`: `Once` `Count(n)` `Forever`.
Keyframes: `Keyframes::new().at(0.0, |k| k.opacity(0.4)).at(1.0, |k| k.opacity(1.0))` + `el.with_keyframes(id, kf, anim)`.
Cancellable: `el.with_cancellable_animation(id, anim, f) -> (el, AnimationHandle)`; `handle.cancel()`.
Elastic scrolling is automatic on macOS for scroll containers; `ScrollHandle::new()` exposes `.offset()` / `.set_offset(point)` / `.max_offset()`. Input gate: prefer `cx.advanced_input_handoff_checked(AdvancedInputHandoffBuilder::new().capability_report(CapabilityReport::current()).pointer_policy(PointerInputPolicyBuilder::drag_surface("canvas")).gesture_policy(GestureInputPolicyBuilder::canvas("canvas")).touch_surface("canvas", 2).stylus_surface("inking", true, true).roadmap_gamepad("native controller input").roadmap_midi("MIDI control surface"))?` before generated games, creative tools, kiosks, or music apps bind handlers; inspect `AdvancedInputHandoff::to_text()` and `AdvancedInputNextAction` without logging surface ids, shortcuts, labels, coordinates, raw event payloads, device ids, gamepad/MIDI names, or roadmap text. Use hosted input islands only when browser DOM input semantics are the dependency.

## Canvas & graphics

Immediate-mode: prefer `canvas(size, |draw, win, app| { draw.fill_rect(bounds, color); tracing::info!(summary = draw.to_text(), "canvas draw"); })` for generated charts/timelines/custom controls, inspecting `command_count()`, `path_count()`, `quad_count()`, `filled_quad_count()`, `stroked_quad_count()`, `text_count()`, `image_count()`, `state_stack_depth()`, and `is_empty()` without logging text, image data, colors, or coordinates; raw two-pass `canvas(|bounds, win, app| { prepaint }, |bounds, state, win, app| { win.paint_quad(fill(bounds, color)); win.paint_path(path, color); })` remains available.
Paths: `PathBuilder::fill()` or `PathBuilder::stroke(px(N))` → `.move_to(p)` `.line_to(p)` `.curve_to(to, ctrl)` `.cubic_curve_to(to, c1, c2)` `.close()` `.build()?`.
Gradients (pass to `.bg`): `linear_gradient(angle, linear_color_stop(rgb(..), 0.0), linear_color_stop(rgb(..), 1.0))`, also `radial_gradient`, `conic_gradient`, `multi_stop_linear_gradient`.
SVG: `svg().path("icon.svg").size(px(N)).text_color(rgb(..))`. Native motion: inspect `Animation::to_text()`, `AnimationSequence::to_text()`, `Keyframes::to_text()`, `StyledKeyframe::to_text()`, `KeyframeTrack::to_text()`, `MediaKeyframe::to_text()`, `Repeat::to_text()`, and `Easing::to_text()` for timeline/curve/repeat/keyframe/property/interpolation counts without opacity/transform/media values, exact keyframe times, custom callbacks, or bezier points. Lottie: prefer native `lottie(src).autoplay().loop_forever()` for animated vector assets; inspect `LottieSource::to_text()`, `LottieAnimation::to_text()`, `LottiePlayer::to_text()`, and element `to_text()` for source/playback/prefetch/loading/fallback summaries without paths, URLs, embedded names, bytes, or fallback text.
Capability gate: prefer `cx.graphics_canvas_handoff_checked(GraphicsCanvasHandoffBuilder::new().capability_report(graphics_capability_report()).interactive_native_canvas("timeline").svg_assets(3).lottie_animations(1).effect_layers(2).headless_render_evidence(1).browser_graphics_island("webgl").roadmap_custom_shader("native shader plugin"))?` before generated visual apps choose canvas/SVG/Lottie/effect/headless/WebView/roadmap routes; inspect `GraphicsCanvasHandoff::to_text()` and `GraphicsCanvasNextAction` without logging surface IDs, asset names, shader code, coordinates, colors, image bytes, or WebView IDs. `graphics_capability_report()` exposes `GraphicsCapabilityStatus::{Full, Partial, WebView, Roadmap}`; do not promise public native WebGL/WebGPU/custom-shader parity while `public_render_targets` or `public_custom_shaders` are `Roadmap`; use explicit browser graphics islands only for browser-owned canvas/WebGL/WebGPU semantics.

## Actions & keybindings

Define: `actions!(namespace, [Save, Undo, Redo])`.
Bind once at startup: prefer `let builder = KeyBindingSetBuilder::new().binding("cmd-s", Save).binding_with_context("tab", Tab, Some("Editor")); tracing::info!(summary = builder.to_text(), "keymap"); let plan = cx.key_bindings_checked(builder)?` to preview builder binding/context/platform-mapped counts plus normalized shortcuts/action names/context counts and `plan.to_text()` before `cx.bind_keys_checked(...)`; raw `cx.bind_keys([KeyBinding::new("cmd-s", Save, None), KeyBinding::new("tab", Tab, Some("Editor"))])` remains available (3rd arg = optional key context).
Command registry: prefer `registry.register_action_checked("editor.save", "Save", || { ... })?` or `registry.register_checked(Box::new(command))?` for command palettes, menus, toolbars, and agent action lists; checked registration rejects empty/padded/overly long/non-portable IDs, invalid names, and duplicate IDs; raw `register(...)` / `register_action(...)` remain available for intentional replacement.
Handle: `div().track_focus(&self.focus_handle).on_action(cx.listener(Self::on_save))`, where `fn on_save(&mut self, _: &Save, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>)`.
Focus: `cx.focus_handle().tab_index(N).tab_stop(true)`; `window.focus(&h)` / `window.focus_next()` / `window.focus_prev()`.
Focus traps: for custom modals/popovers/palettes use `FocusTrapController::modal()` from `kael_ui::prelude`; in `on_key_down`, call `trap.action_for_keystroke(&event.keystroke)` and handle `FocusTrapAction::FocusNext` with `window.focus_next_in_group()`, `FocusPrevious` with `window.focus_prev_in_group()`, and `Dismiss` with the close handler. Use `FocusTrapController::persistent()` or `.dismiss_on_escape(false)` when Escape should not close.
Accessibility: prefer `let handoff = cx.accessibility_automation_handoff_checked(AccessibilityAutomationHandoffBuilder::new().tree(tree).attributes(AccessibilityAttributes::button(label)).action_request(AccessibilityActionRequest::new(node_id, AccessibilityAction::Click)).announcement(status).focus_target(tree, node_id).hosted_dom_automation(surface))?` before exporting trees, routing actions, announcing status, moving focus, or delegating to hosted DOM selectors; inspect `AccessibilityAutomationHandoff`, `AccessibilityAutomationNextAction`, `audits_tree()`, `validates_attributes()`, `routes_action_request()`, `announces_status()`, `focuses_node()`, `uses_hosted_dom_automation()`, and `to_text()` without logging labels, values, URLs, selectors, payload text, audit messages, or geometry; for custom interactive `div()` controls use semantic recipes such as `AccessibilityAttributes::button(label)`, `.switch(label, on)`, `.checkbox(label, checked)`, `.link(label)`, `.slider(label, current, min, max, step)`, then call `attrs.validate()?` before `.accessibility(attrs)`; use `let report = attrs.audit_report(); tracing::info!(summary = report.to_text(), "accessibility audit")` for non-throwing component reviews and `AccessibilityTree::audit_report()` before platform export when agents need all issues at once, including missing names/actions, invalid range values, conflicting states, hidden focused nodes, missing children, parent mismatches, multiple focused nodes, and unknown roles; inspect `issue_count()`, `error_count()`, `warning_count()`, `is_ready()`, and `summary()` for generated fallback UI; use `AccessibilityActionRouter`, `Window::on_accessibility_action(...)`, `AccessibilityAnnouncementBuilder`, and `AccessibilityFocusBuilder` for DOM-like action, live-region, and focus handoffs; inspect semantic `MenuEntry`/`Link`/`TreeItem`/`Navigator` and accessibility `to_text()` summaries; drop to `AccessibilityAttributes::new(AccessibilityRole::...)` only for custom roles/states.
Assistive actions: advertise actions with `.action(AccessibilityAction::...)` / `.actions(...)`; normalize platform callbacks with `AccessibilityActionRequest::from_accesskit_for_node(node_id, &node, action)` or `from_accesskit_for_node_with_data(...)`, and route app handlers through `Window::on_accessibility_action(...)` or `AccessibilityActionRouter::on_action(...)` / `.dispatch(...)`. macOS/Linux adapter drains normalize pending AccessKit requests against the current tree and `Window::drain_accessibility_actions()` exposes delivered requests after platform tree updates. Windows feeds UIA focus, invoke, toggle, expand/collapse, value, and range-value pattern calls into the same window route; exact edits arrive as `AccessibilityAction::SetValue` with `AccessibilityActionPayload::Value(text)` or `AccessibilityActionPayload::NumericValue(value)`.
File drops: prefer `let filter = FileDropFilter::images().max_files(4)` / `.audio()` / `.video()` / `.media()` / `.single_file()`, then `div().can_drop_external(filter.clone()).on_external_drop(move |data, _, _| { tracing::info!(summary = filter.to_text(), "file drop filter"); tracing::info!(summary = data.to_text(), "external drop"); if let Some(paths) = data.accepted_paths_by(&filter) { ... }; for url in data.urls() { ... }; if let Some(text) = data.text_value() { ... } })`; use `FileDropFilter::new().extensions([...])` for custom extension sets. Pure file drops stay as `ExternalPaths` internally for compatibility, but `on_external_drop` normalizes them to `ExternalDropData`; inspect `ExternalDropData::to_text()`, `ExternalPaths::to_text()`, `FileDropFilter::to_text()`, and `FileDropMatch::to_text()` for path/text/URL/accept/reject counts without logging paths, filenames, text, URLs, or extension labels. For custom drag bridges/tests, use `ExternalDropData::from_drag_value(value)`, `ExternalDropData::from_paths(...).with_text(...).with_url(...)`, `ExternalDropData::from_uri_list(text_uri_list)`, or `ExternalDropData::from_plain_text(text)`. macOS/Windows native text or URL drops and Linux URI-list drops emit `ExternalDropData` when non-file data is present.

## Platform APIs

Before depending on OS features, use `CapabilityReport::current()`. `report.require(PlatformFeature::WebView)?` requires full support; `report.require_available(feature)?` and `report.is_available(feature)` accept `Full`, `Partial`, or `RequiresInit`; `CapabilityCheck::new().require(...).require_available(...).prefer_available(...).evaluate(&report)` returns missing required/preferred items plus readable `required_failure_summary()` text for startup gates and fallbacks. For broad native capability audits inspect `coverage_summary().to_text()`, `full_features()`, `available_features()`, `partial_features()`, `requires_init_features()`, `unsupported_features()`, `fallback_risk_features()`, and `fallback_risk_summary()`. For input-heavy apps, require `PlatformFeature::PrecisionPointerInput` and prefer-available `GestureInput`, `TouchInput`, and `PenInput`; provide mouse/keyboard controls when preferred touch/pen/gesture support is missing or partial. For frameless/custom titlebars, inspect `WindowControls::to_text()`, `TitlebarOptions::to_text()`, `ResizeEdge::to_text()`, and `WindowControlArea::to_text()` / `is_drag_region()` / `is_button()` before dispatching `WindowChromeCommand`, without logging titles or traffic-light/menu coordinates.

| API | Usage |
|-----|-------|
| File dialog | For Desktop `showOpenDialog`/`showSaveDialog` parity, prefer `let handoff = cx.file_dialog_handoff_checked(FileDialogHandoffBuilder::new().open(OpenDialogBuilder::files().image_files().filter("Markdown", ["md", "markdown"]).prompt(label)).save(SaveDialogBuilder::new(dir).suggested_name(name).default_extension("pdf")).hosted_file_picker(surface_id).roadmap_work(reason))?; tracing::info!(summary = handoff.to_text(), next = ?handoff.next_action(), "file dialog handoff")` before generated apps choose native open/save, raw `PathPromptOptions`, hosted picker islands, or tracked roadmap work; use `cx.open_dialog_checked(...)` / `cx.save_dialog_checked(...)`, then `cx.show_open_dialog(...).await??`, `OpenDialogBuilder::directory().multiple(true)`, and `cx.show_save_dialog(...).await??` for direct native UI; use `FileDialogFilter::{images,audio,video,pdf,text}()` or `.filter(name, extensions)` for open-dialog filters, inspect `FileDialogFilter::to_text()`, `extension_count()`, `OpenDialogPlan::filter_extension_count()`, `OpenDialogBuilder::to_text()`, `PathPromptOptions::to_text()`, `FileDialogHandoff::to_text()`, and `FileDialogNextAction` for path-safe routing summaries, and use `.pdf()`, `.text()`, `.json()`, or `.default_extension(ext)` for save-name defaults; checked handoffs/builders reject incoherent open modes, invalid filter names/extensions, empty/padded/control-character prompt labels, invalid hosted picker IDs, empty roadmap notes, empty save directories, unsafe suggested names, and malformed default extensions without logging labels, filter names, suggested names, hosted IDs, roadmap text, paths, or selected values; raw `prompt_for_paths(PathPromptOptions { ... })` / `prompt_for_new_path(...)` remain available |
| File drops | Prefer UI `FileDropFilter::images()/audio()/video()/media()/single_file()` for hover acceptance, then `cx.data_transfer_drop_intake_checked(DataTransferDropIntakePlanBuilder::new(drop_data).file_filter(filter.clone()).max_urls(2).max_text_bytes(16384).allow_missing_paths())?` for DataTransfer-style paths/text/URLs/mixed payload routing before state changes, then `cx.file_drop_intent_checked(FileDropIntentBuilder::media_source().paths(paths).max_paths(count).canonicalize_paths())?` or `.open_document()`, `.import_files()`, `.import_folder()`, `.project_workspace()` after drop before import/open work; prefer `DataTransferDropIntakePlanBuilder` plus `DataTransferDropIntakeNextAction` before accepting paths URLs text mixed payloads unknown files or hosted fallback, and prefer `DragDropTransferHandoffBuilder::{incoming_drop, media_drop, file_export_drag, generated_file_export, internal_drag, hosted_data_transfer}()` / `DragDropTransferHandoff` when generated builders or AI agents need one checked descriptor across incoming drops, outbound file-export drags, internal drag routing, and hosted DOM `DataTransfer` delegation, then inspect `DragDropTransferNextAction` before accepting drops or starting drag work; checked intake validates drop emptiness, filters, max URL counts, text byte limits, mixed payload policy, unknown path policy, hosted ids, semantic purpose, non-empty paths, file-vs-directory policy, extension allowlists, max path count, optional existence, canonicalization, and deduplication; use builder `to_text()`, configured counts, intake `to_text()`, `file_intake()`, `can_route_immediately()`, handoff `to_text()`, `is_incoming_drop()`, `is_file_export_drag()`, `is_internal_drag()`, `is_hosted_data_transfer()`, and intent `to_text()` / `path_count()` for path-safe agent summaries without logging paths, file names, text, URLs, MIME strings, generated bytes, route ids, WebView ids, coordinates, selectors, hosted ids, or payload contents |
| File export drags | Prefer `let export = cx.file_export_drag_checked(FileExportDragIntentBuilder::generated_files(reason).virtual_file_with_mime(name, mime, bytes))?` for desktop-app file promises / drag-to-desktop generated artifacts, or `.existing_files(reason).path(path)` for dragging existing files; inspect `item_count()`, `display_names()`, `existing_path_count()`, and `virtual_file_count()` before native drag handoff; gate backends with `PlatformFeature::FileExportDrag`; existing-path exports require and preflight `Capability::FilesystemRead { scope: PathScope::UserSelected }`, while generated virtual files require no filesystem capability; checked intents validate purpose text, item count, safe file names, MIME type shape, non-empty generated bytes, byte limits, optional existing-path presence, and duplicate path items |
| File intake | Prefer `let handoff = cx.workspace_open_handoff_checked(WorkspaceOpenHandoffBuilder::paths(paths).canonicalize_paths().watch_depth(2))?` when dialogs, drops, recent docs, or file deep links may open projects, documents, media, archives, and watcher roots together; inspect `WorkspaceOpenNextAction`, `intake()`, `watch_set()`, `workspace_entry_count()`, `watch_root_count()`, `needs_unknown_review()`, `can_open_known_entries()`, and `to_text()` before mutating project state or registering watchers. For app-owned storage/project metadata/index/cache/export mutation, prefer `let ops = cx.file_operation_handoff_checked(FileOperationHandoffBuilder::new().read(AppPathRole::Config, "settings.json").write(AppPathRole::Data, "projects/index.json").copy(AppPathRole::Data, "projects/index.json", AppPathRole::Cache, "snapshots/index.json").move_path(AppPathRole::Cache, "snapshots/index.json", AppPathRole::Cache, "snapshots/latest.json").delete(AppPathRole::Temp, "exports/draft.tmp").hosted_file_manager("cloud-drive"))?`, then inspect `FileOperationNextAction` and `ops.to_text()` without logging paths, filenames, file contents, hosted ids, or roadmap text; for classification only, use `cx.file_intake_plan_checked(FileIntakePlanBuilder::new().paths(paths).canonicalize_paths())?`; checked plans validate non-empty paths, optional existence, max path count, canonicalization, deduplication, normalized extensions, unknown-kind handling, scoped app path roles, relative operation paths, overwrite/create-parent policy, and byte budgets |
| Message dialog | Prefer `let prompts = cx.message_dialog_handoff_checked(MessageDialogHandoffBuilder::new().message(MessageDialogBuilder::info(title, message)).confirm(MessageDialogBuilder::confirm(title, message)).destructive_confirm(MessageDialogBuilder::destructive_confirm(title, message, "Delete")).unsaved_changes(MessageDialogBuilder::save_discard_cancel(title, message)).hosted_browser_dialog("beforeunload"))?` before generated alert/confirm/destructive/unsaved/about/hosted prompt side effects; inspect `MessageDialogNextAction` and `MessageDialogHandoff::to_text()` without logging titles, messages, detail text, labels, app names, versions, document names, paths, URLs, hosted ids, prompt inputs, business payloads, or roadmap text; lower-level path remains `let plan = cx.message_dialog_checked(MessageDialogBuilder::save_discard_cancel(title, message))?; tracing::info!(summary = plan.to_text(), "message dialog")`, then `cx.show_message_dialog(MessageDialogBuilder::info(title, message))?`, `MessageDialogBuilder::confirm(title, message).detail(text)`, `MessageDialogBuilder::destructive_confirm(title, message, "Delete")`, `MessageDialogBuilder::save_discard_cancel(title, message)`, or `MessageDialogBuilder::error(title, message)`; use `.default_button(index)` / `.cancel_button(index)` for custom button order, and `MessageDialogBuilder::to_text()` / `DialogOptions::to_text()` for label-safe summaries before lower-level dispatch; checked builders reject empty, padded, control-character, duplicate, too many, and overly long generated labels; result is a button-index receiver matching the configured button order; raw `show_dialog(DialogOptions { ... })` remains available |
| Menus | For Desktop Edit menu parity, app-menu roles, and generated context-menu flows, prefer `let handoff = cx.menu_command_handoff_checked(MenuCommandHandoffBuilder::new().menu_bar(MenuBarBuilder::new().menu(MenuBuilder::new(name).action(label, action).separator().submenu(...)).menu(MenuBuilder::standard_edit("Edit", undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, select_all))).context_menu(NativeContextMenuBuilder::new().action(label, id)).edit_command_snapshot().hosted_context_menu(surface_id).roadmap_work(reason))?; tracing::info!(summary = handoff.to_text(), next = ?handoff.next_action(), "menu command handoff")` before generated apps install app menus, show context menus, snapshot edit commands, delegate hosted context-menu semantics, or track menu parity; use `cx.edit_command_state_snapshot_checked()?` before browser selection APIs and `cx.menu_bar_checked(...)` / `cx.set_menus_checked(...)` for direct native app-menu installs; inspect `MenuCommandNextAction`, `MenuCommandHandoff::to_text()`, `MenuBuilder::to_text()`, `MenuBarBuilder::to_text()`, `MenuBarPlan::to_text()`, `item_count()`, `action_count()`, `has_os_actions()`, and `has_system_menus()` for content-safe audit lines; standard Edit menus get native Undo/Redo/Cut/Copy/Paste/Select All role mappings and checked handoffs/builders reject empty/padded/control-character/overly long labels, invalid hosted surface IDs, empty roadmap notes, empty menus, duplicate top-level menu names, empty context menus, and ambiguous context action IDs without logging labels, action IDs, hosted IDs, roadmap text, or edit labels; raw `set_menus(...)`, `Vec<Menu>`, and `MenuItem::...` remain available |
| Context menu | Prefer `cx.show_context_menu_checked(position, NativeContextMenuBuilder::new().action(label, id).separator().toggle(label, checked, id).submenu(label, items), \|id, cx\| { ... })?` so empty labels/IDs, empty submenus, and duplicate action IDs are rejected before callbacks become ambiguous; inspect `NativeContextMenuBuilder::to_text()` and item/action/toggle/checked-toggle/submenu/separator counts without logging labels or action IDs; raw `show_context_menu(...)` and `Vec<TrayMenuItem>` remain available |
| System tray | Prefer `let shell = cx.desktop_shell_chrome_handoff_checked(DesktopShellChromeHandoffBuilder::new().runtime_snapshot(AppRuntimeSnapshotQueryBuilder::new().require_not_quitting()).tray_app(TrayAppBuilder::new().action(label, id).separator().toggle(label, checked, id).status_tooltip(text).panel().keep_alive_without_windows(true)).window_placement(WindowPlacementBuilder::new(size(px(360.), px(240.)))).progress_indicator(ProgressIndicatorBuilder::normal(scope, 0.5).window()).dock_badge(DockBadgeBuilder::count(count)).user_attention(UserAttentionBuilder::informational().reason(reason)))?` before generated tray/background apps, panels, taskbar/dock progress, badges, and attention requests mutate platform chrome; inspect `DesktopShellChromeNextAction` and `shell.to_text()` without logging labels, action IDs, tooltip text, progress scopes, badge labels, attention reasons, geometry, or roadmap text; lower-level tray path remains `let tray_builder = TrayAppBuilder::new().action(label, id).separator().toggle(label, checked, id).status_tooltip(text).panel().keep_alive_without_windows(true); tracing::info!(summary = tray_builder.to_text(), "tray app"); let tray = cx.tray_app_checked(tray_builder)?` then `cx.configure_tray_app_checked(...)`; use `cx.set_tray_icon_checked(TrayIconBuilder::png(bytes))?` / `.ico(bytes)` / `.bytes(bytes)` / `.clear()`, `cx.set_tray_menu_checked(TrayMenuBuilder::new().action(label, id).separator().toggle(label, checked, id).submenu(label, items))?`, `NativeContextMenuBuilder`, and `cx.set_tray_tooltip_checked(TrayTooltipBuilder::status(text))?` when pieces are owned separately; checked paths reject invalid runtime state, placement, progress, badges, icon buffers, empty labels/IDs, empty submenus, duplicate action IDs, and empty/padded/control-character/overly long tooltips; raw `set_tray_icon(...)`, `set_tray_menu(...)`, `Vec<TrayMenuItem>`, `set_tray_tooltip(...)`, and `set_keep_alive_without_windows(...)` remain available |
| Clipboard | Prefer `cx.write_clipboard_text_checked(text)?` for generated/plain text writes and `let read = ClipboardReadRequestBuilder::text(reason); tracing::info!(summary = read.to_text(), "clipboard read"); cx.read_clipboard_text_checked(read)?` for generated/plain text reads; use raw `cx.write_clipboard_text(text)` / `cx.read_clipboard_text()?` only for already-validated flows; prefer `cx.write_clipboard_html(plain_text, html)?` or `ClipboardItem::builder().html(plain_text, html)?` for desktop-app rich HTML with a plain-text fallback; prefer `let item = ClipboardItem::builder().try_text_with_json_metadata(text, metadata)?.image_ref(&image); tracing::info!(summary = item.to_text(), "clipboard write"); cx.write_clipboard_item_checked(item)?` for rich text/image/metadata payloads when metadata may fail to serialize, and `ClipboardReadRequestBuilder::{html, image, any}(reason)` with `cx.read_clipboard_item_checked(read)?` for Desktop `clipboard.readHTML()` / `readImage()` style reads; prefer `ClipboardEditingHandoffBuilder::{write, write_text, read_text, read_any, clear, snapshot_edit_commands}()` / `ClipboardEditingHandoff` when generated builders or AI agents need one checked descriptor across clipboard write/read/clear and edit-command snapshot flows, then inspect `ClipboardEditingNextAction` before touching user-visible state; checked writes reject empty items, empty text, empty metadata, empty image bytes, empty HTML, and NUL/control characters and require `Capability::ClipboardWrite`; checked reads reject invalid reasons or missing expected formats and require `Capability::ClipboardRead`; inspect builders or reads with `to_text()`, `entry_count()`, `text_count()`, `image_count()`, `metadata_count()`, `text_len_bytes()`, `has_text()`, `has_html()`, `has_image()`, handoff `to_text()`, `is_write()`, `is_read()`, `is_clear()`, and `is_edit_snapshot()` for content-safe agent summaries, plus `item.text()`, `item.html()`, `item.strings()`, `ClipboardString::metadata()`, `ClipboardString::html()`, `item.images()`, and `item.first_image()` after reads; runtime `Image` exposes `format()`, `byte_len()`, `has_bytes()`, and byte-safe `to_text()` for native-image payload summaries; use `let clear = ClipboardClearBuilder::new(reason); tracing::info!(summary = clear.to_text(), "clipboard clear"); cx.clear_clipboard_checked(clear)?` for Desktop `clipboard.clear()`-style privacy/reset flows without logging reason text; raw `cx.write_clipboard_text(text)`, `cx.write_clipboard_item(...)`, `cx.write_to_clipboard(ClipboardItem::...)`, and `cx.read_from_clipboard()?` remain available |
| Share sheet | With the `share` feature, prefer `let builder = ShareSheet::builder().subject(title).text(text).url(url).file(path).exclude(ShareType::Social); tracing::info!(summary = builder.to_text(), "share sheet builder"); let sheet = builder.build_checked()?; tracing::info!(summary = sheet.to_text(), "share sheet"); cx.show_share_sheet_checked(sheet).await?` or `cx.show_share_sheet(...)` for OS share/export handoff; use `ShareItem::{text,url,file,files,image}` and `ShareSheet::{text,url,file,files}` for one-line payloads; checked builders reject empty payloads, URL values without schemes, empty image MIME/bytes, and missing files before invoking platform share UI; inspect `ShareItem::to_text()`, `ShareImage::to_text()`, `ShareSheetBuilder::to_text()`, `sheet.to_text()`, `sheet.item_summaries()`, `cx.share_support().to_text()`, and `ShareResult::to_text()` for destination support, payload shape, completion, and item/text/url/file/image/exclusion counts without logging text bodies, URLs, paths, subjects, MIME strings, suggested names, or platform activity ids |
| Secure credentials | Prefer `let handoff = cx.secure_credential_handoff_checked(SecureCredentialHandoffBuilder::new(cx.current_process_id()).feature_preflight(CapabilityReport::current()).permission_broker(PermissionBrokerInstallBuilder::new().deny_ungranted()).write(CredentialBuilder::new(service).username(account).password(secret)).read(CredentialServiceBuilder::new(service)).delete(CredentialServiceBuilder::new(service)).support_diagnostics(SupportDiagnosticsBuilder::new()).hosted_auth_profile("browser-login-profile").roadmap_work("native passkey credential recipe"))?` before platform keychain / credential-manager writes, reads, deletes, login/logout cleanup, hosted auth fallback, or diagnostics; inspect `SecureCredentialNextAction` and `handoff.to_text()` without logging service keys, usernames, token values, secret bytes, hosted profile IDs, account IDs, or roadmap text; checked handoffs reject unavailable keychains, unsafe broker setup, empty/padded/control-character/overlong service/user values, empty secrets, invalid hosted profile IDs, and unsafe roadmap text; lower-level `CredentialBuilder`, `CredentialServiceBuilder`, checked secure credential read/write/delete calls, and raw `write_credentials(...)`/`read_credentials(...)`/`delete_credentials(...)` remain available for hand-validated integrations |
| Permissions | For Desktop `media capture`/`mediaDevices` parity, preflight native consent and package rationale before source queries; prefer `let request = PermissionRequestBuilder::startup_privacy(); let plan = request.plan_against_manifest(&privacy_manifest)?; tracing::info!(summary = plan.to_text(), "permission setup plan"); let permissions = cx.request_permissions(request)?; tracing::info!(summary = permissions.to_text(), "permission preflight")` for accessibility + media startup checks, `.capture_studio()` for capture/recording tools, or `.media_devices()` for microphone + camera only; use `AppPrivacyManifestBuilder` plus `plan_against_manifest(...)` before prompting so generated apps catch missing camera, microphone, or screen-capture rationale; inspect `PermissionPreflightPlan::{missing_manifest_permissions,missing_manifest_count,manifest_complete,requires_manifest_update,to_text}` and request `requested_permission_count()`, `requested_privacy_permissions()`, and `to_text()` before showing setup UI; inspect result `requested_permissions()`, `granted_permissions()`, `pending_permissions()`, `has_pending_permission()`, `all_granted()`, `blocking_denials()`, `granted_summary()`, `blocking_denial_summary()`, and `to_text()` before starting blocked features; use `.microphone_with_callback(...)` / `.camera_with_callback(...)` for OS prompt results |
| Shell | For Desktop shell parity, use `ShellTargetsBuilder` plus checked capabilities before hosted helpers; prefer `cx.open_external_url(url)?`, `cx.open_path(path)?`, `cx.show_item_in_folder(path)?`, or `cx.open_shell_target(ShellTarget::...)`; use `let shell = ShellTargetsBuilder::new().url(help_url).reveal_path(report_path).require_existing_paths(); tracing::info!(summary = shell.to_text(), "shell targets"); let plan = cx.shell_targets_checked(shell)?` to preview target kinds and required URL/shell capabilities before side effects, then `cx.open_shell_targets(...)` to dispatch; use `let trash = cx.trash_request_checked(TrashRequest::builder(path).canonicalize_path())?` to preview Desktop `shell.trashItem(...)` style move-to-trash handoffs, inspect `trash.display_name()`, `parent_path()`, `requires_shell_execute()`, and content-safe `to_text()` before dispatch without logging target paths or filenames, then call `cx.trash_item_checked(TrashRequest::builder(path).canonicalize_path())?` after confirmation to validate, capability-check, and dispatch to the platform trash/recycle hook; checked shell targets reject empty/padded URLs, unsupported shell URL schemes, missing HTTP(S) hosts, empty paths, and NUL characters; trash requests additionally reject filesystem roots, relative paths unless opted in, and missing targets by default; use `.canonicalize_paths()` when generated path/reveal targets should be normalized; shell URL targets allow `http`, `https`, and `mailto`, while custom app schemes should use deep-link registration; path/reveal/trash actions require `ShellExecute` |
| App paths | Prefer `let paths_builder = AppPathBuilder::new(app_id).all_common().create_dirs(); tracing::info!(summary = paths_builder.to_text(), "app path builder"); let paths = cx.app_paths_checked(paths_builder)?; tracing::info!(summary = paths.to_text(), "app paths")` for Desktop `app path lookup`-style data/config/cache/log/temp/download locations; inspect `data_dir()`, `config_dir()`, `cache_dir()`, `logs_dir()`, `temp_dir()`, `downloads_dir()`, `role_count()`, `has_role(...)`, `app_scoped_role_count()`, and `user_global_role_count()`; summaries report role coverage and create-dir intent without logging app ids or absolute paths; checked paths reject empty, padded, whitespace/control-character, separator-containing, and duplicate-role app path requests before storage, migrations, logs, downloads, or plugins start |

| User attention | Prefer `let plan = UserAttentionBuilder::informational().reason(reason).build_plan_checked()?; let request = cx.request_user_attention_plan_checked(plan)?; request.cancel(cx)` for dock/taskbar bounce/flash flows with generated reasons; inspect `plan.is_informational()`, `is_critical()`, `has_reason()`, and `to_text()` before dispatch, and `request.to_text()` after dispatch; use `UserAttentionBuilder::critical()` for urgent conditions; raw `cx.request_user_attention(AttentionType::...)`, `cx.request_user_attention_with(...)`, and `cx.cancel_user_attention()` remain available |
| Dock | Prefer `let badge = DockBadgeBuilder::count(count); tracing::info!(summary = badge.to_text(), "dock badge"); cx.set_dock_badge_checked(badge)?`, `DockBadgeBuilder::label(label)`, and `DockBadgeBuilder::clear()` for dock/taskbar badges so empty, padded, control-character, and overly long generated labels fail before platform rendering; inspect `has_label()`, `is_clear()`, and `is_count()` without logging badge text or count values; use `cx.set_dock_menu_checked(DockMenuBuilder::new().action(label, action).separator().submenu(...))?` and `cx.perform_dock_menu_action_checked(DockMenuActionBuilder::new(index))?` so empty/separator-only menus, empty submenu trees, padded labels, invalid action indexes, control characters, and overly long labels fail before native installation/dispatch; prefer `let recents = RecentDocumentsBuilder::new().require_existing_files().canonicalize().document(path).document(other_path); tracing::info!(summary = recents.to_text(), "recent documents"); let plan = cx.recent_documents_checked(recents.clone())?; cx.add_recent_documents(recents)?` for OS recent-document lists when paths should be real files; inspect `plan.documents()`, `document_count()`, and content-safe `to_text()` before OS state changes, and use `RecentDocumentsClearBuilder::new(reason).to_text()` / `has_reason()` before clearing without logging reason text; use `let jump = JumpListBuilder::new().action(label, action).workspace_path(project); tracing::info!(summary = jump.to_text(), "jump list"); let plan = cx.jump_list_checked(jump)?; cx.update_jump_list_plan_checked(plan)` for taskbar launcher/recent workspace groups before OS mutation; raw `set_dock_badge(Some(label))`, `set_dock_badge(None)`, `set_dock_menu(items)`, and `add_recent_document(path)` remain available |
| Jump lists | Prefer `let jump = JumpListBuilder::new().action(label, action).workspace_path(project).workspace([folder, workspace_file]); tracing::info!(summary = jump.to_text(), "jump list"); let plan = cx.jump_list_checked(jump)?; cx.update_jump_list_plan_checked(plan)` for Windows taskbar jump lists and recent workspace groups; inspect builder/plan `task_count()`, `workspace_count()`, `workspace_path_count()`, and content-safe `to_text()` before OS state changes without logging action labels or workspace paths; use `.require_existing_paths().canonicalize()` when entries must be real paths; `cx.update_jump_list_checked(builder)?` remains available for direct validate-and-apply; checked paths reject empty lists, non-action task items, empty/padded action labels, empty workspace entries, and empty paths; raw `update_jump_list(menus, entries)` remains available |
| Single instance | Prefer `let launch = SingleInstanceBuilder::new(app_id).launch()?; tracing::info!(summary = launch.to_text(), "single-instance launch"); match launch { SingleInstanceLaunch::Primary(instance) => { instance.on_activate(Box::new(|| { ... })); }, SingleInstanceLaunch::Duplicate { .. } => return Ok(()), }`; inspect `app_id()`, `is_primary()`, `is_duplicate()`, `notified_existing()`, and `to_text()` for startup telemetry; builder validation rejects empty, padded, control-character, path-like, and overly long app IDs before platform lock names are created; raw `SingleInstance::acquire(app_id)` and `send_activate_to_existing(app_id)?` remain available |
| Biometric | Prefer `let request = cx.authenticate_biometric_with(BiometricAuthBuilder::unlock_vault(), \|ok\| { ... })?; tracing::info!(summary = request.to_text(), "biometric authentication")`, `BiometricAuthBuilder::approve_payment()`, or `BiometricAuthBuilder::new(reason)` for custom copy so empty/padded/control-character/overly long prompt reasons are rejected and unavailable devices skip prompting by default; inspect `status()`, `available()`, `kind()`, `prompted()`, and `to_text()` for password/PIN fallback; raw `cx.biometric_status()` and `cx.authenticate_biometric(...)` remain available |
| Screen/media capture | Prefer `let manager = cx.capture_manager(); let query = CaptureSourceQueryBuilder::screens_and_windows().name_contains("Display").limit(4); tracing::info!(summary = query.to_text(), "capture source query"); let sources = manager.sources(query)?; tracing::info!(summary = sources.to_text(), "capture sources"); let handoff = cx.capture_handoff_checked(CaptureHandoffBuilder::screen_share_with_microphone().auto_start(true))?; tracing::info!(summary = handoff.to_text(), "capture handoff"); match handoff.next_action() { CaptureHandoffNextAction::PreflightPermissions => ..., CaptureHandoffNextAction::ShowSourcePicker => ..., CaptureHandoffNextAction::ResolveCaptureConfigs => ..., CaptureHandoffNextAction::StartCapturePipeline => ... }` for Desktop `media capture`/`desktopCapturer`-style source catalogs, consent, picker, config, and coordinated screen/mic/camera/system-audio capture without hand-written session loops; use `manager.pipeline_checked(...)` when the app wants to inspect or configure the `CapturePipeline` before starting, or `handoff.start_pipeline_checked(&manager, callback)` when the checked handoff is ready to run; use `CaptureSourceQueryBuilder::{screens, windows, screens_and_windows, cameras, microphones, system_audio}()` for picker metadata with checked kinds, availability filtering, name filters, unavailable-source inclusion, and result limits; inspect `CaptureSourceQueryBuilder::to_text()`, `CaptureSourceCatalog::to_text()`, `CaptureDeviceInfo::to_text()`, `CaptureConfigBuilder::to_text()`, `CaptureConfig::to_text()`, `CaptureConfigSetBuilder::to_text()`, `CaptureHandoff::to_text()`, `kind_count(...)`, `available_count()`, `unavailable_count()`, `source_count()`, `has_video()`, `has_audio()`, `required_consents()`, and `requires_consent(...)` before dispatch so generated agents can summarize source kinds/counts/options without logging device IDs, device/window names, name filters, or exact resolution values; use `CaptureConfigSetBuilder::{screen_with_microphone, camera_with_microphone, screen_with_system_audio}()` or `CaptureHandoffBuilder::{screen_share_with_microphone, camera_call, screen_recording_with_system_audio}()` for common grouped flows, or `CaptureConfigBuilder::{screen, window, camera, microphone, system_audio}()`, `.device_name_contains(...)`, and `.device_id(...)` for single-source/session flows; raw `CaptureConfig::new(...)`, `manager.configs(...)`, `manager.create_session_with(...)`, `manager.devices(kind)`, `cx.is_screen_capture_supported()`, and `cx.screen_capture_sources()` remain available for platform source metadata/custom pickers |
| Settings | Prefer `SettingsStore::<AppSettings>::builder(settings_path).migration(...).load_checked()?` or `SettingsStore::new_checked(settings_path)?` for typed JSON app preferences; checked paths reject empty/control-character paths, directory targets, invalid existing parents, zero-version migrations, and duplicate migration target versions before atomic saves; raw `SettingsStore::new(...)`, `SettingsStore::load(...)`, and builder `.load()` remain available when the app owns filesystem validation |
| Undo/redo | Prefer `history.begin_transaction_checked("move selected layers")?; history.push(change); history.end_transaction_checked()?` for grouped editor/design-tool history; inspect `history.to_text()`, `undo_count()`, `redo_count()`, `transaction_change_count()`, `is_at_max_depth()`, and `has_open_transaction()` for menus, command palettes, autosave prompts, and agents without logging descriptions or document content; checked transactions reject nested begins, missing ends, empty/padded/control-character/overly long descriptions; raw `begin_transaction(...)` / `end_transaction()` remain available |
| Background jobs | Prefer `let descriptor = JobDescriptor::new("export/video").with_priority(JobPriority::High).with_retry_policy(policy); tracing::info!(summary = descriptor.to_text(), "background job"); scheduler.schedule_with_descriptor_checked(job, descriptor)?` or `schedule_checked(job)?` for queued worker/background work; checked scheduling rejects invalid job IDs, descriptor/job ID mismatches, self-dependencies, duplicate/invalid dependency IDs, and invalid retry policies before queue mutation; inspect `JobPriority::key()`, `RetryPolicy::to_text()`, `JobDescriptor::{has_retry_policy,dependency_count,is_cancelled,to_text}`, `JobStatus::{key,is_active,is_terminal,to_text}`, `JobProgress::{has_message,to_text}`, and `JobInfo::{has_progress,has_started,has_completed,to_text}` for generated dashboards, logs, and agents without logging job ids, dependency ids, progress messages, exact percentages, retry attempts, or timings; raw `schedule(...)` / `schedule_with_descriptor(...)` remain available when the app owns validation |

## Multi-process & IPC

Host: `WorkerHost::with_temp_dir()`; prefer `ProcessInfoBuilder::worker(ProcessId(0), "name").executable(path).require_existing_executable().build_checked()?` and `ProcessSpawnOptionsBuilder::new().restart_on_failure(3, duration).heartbeat_interval(duration).missed_heartbeats_before_unhealthy(3).build_checked()?`; call `host.spawn_worker_with_options(ProcessClass::Worker, info, options)?` or `host.spawn_worker(ProcessClass::Worker, info)?` for the default bounded-restart policy. Raw `ProcessInfo::worker(...).executable(path)` and `ProcessSpawnOptions::new(...)` remain available when the app owns validation. Use `worker.request(json)?` / `.health_check()?` / `.fire_and_forget(json)?`; `host.on_event(|event: SupervisorEvent| { ... })`.
Child binary: `WorkerClient::connect_from_env()?.run(|req, progress| -> Result<WorkerResponse, WorkerError> { ... })`.
Messages: `WorkerRequest::{Ping, Execute { payload }}`, `WorkerResponse::{Pong, Result(value)}`, `WorkerProgress::Update(value)`, `WorkerError::{Execution(String), Cancelled}`. Transport: Unix sockets (macOS/Linux), named pipes (Windows). Prefer `let handoff = cx.background_work_handoff_checked(BackgroundWorkHandoffBuilder::descriptor(JobDescriptor::new(job_id).with_priority(JobPriority::High)))?`; also wrap `BackgroundWorkHandoffBuilder::{job,progress,cancel,pause,resume,worker_pool,helper_process}` builders in `cx.background_work_handoff_checked(...)` before queueing generated work, reporting progress, mutating queue state, using a worker pool, or escalating to a helper process; inspect `BackgroundWorkHandoff`, `BackgroundWorkNextAction`, `is_job()`, `is_progress()`, `is_cancel()`, `is_pause()`, `is_resume()`, `is_worker_pool()`, `is_helper_process()`, and `to_text()` without logging job ids, dependency ids, progress messages, percentages, worker/helper reasons, or payloads. Prefer wrapping `CommandIpcHandoffBuilder::{register_command,palette_descriptor,ipc_request,ipc_response,ipc_progress,ipc_cancel,extension_rpc,hosted_bridge}` builders in `cx.command_ipc_handoff_checked(...)` before generated commands, palettes, helper IPC, extension RPC, or hosted bridges dispatch; inspect `CommandIpcHandoff`, `CommandIpcNextAction`, `is_register_command()`, `is_palette_descriptor()`, `is_ipc_request()`, `is_ipc_response()`, `is_ipc_progress()`, `is_ipc_cancel()`, `is_extension_rpc()`, `is_hosted_bridge()`, and `to_text()` without logging command ids, labels, categories, shortcuts, icons, correlation ids, payloads, bridge kinds, or errors. Inspect `IpcMessage::to_text()`, `WorkerRequest::to_text()`, `WorkerResponse::to_text()`, `WorkerProgress::to_text()`, `WorkerError::to_text()`, `BootstrapMessage::to_text()`, `IpcFrameSummary::to_text()` / `frame_summary(frame)`, and extension RPC `ExtensionRequest`/`ExtensionResponse`/`ExtensionNotification`/`ExtensionHandshake`/`ExtensionMessage::to_text()` for desktop-app IPC traces without logging JSON payloads, command IDs, settings keys, panel IDs, capability labels, payload strings, or error messages.

## Extensions

`ExtensionHostRuntime::new(dir, app_id)`; build with `PluginManifest::builder(id, name, version, api_version, entry_point, ExecutionModel::Wasm | ExecutionModel::ExternalProcess).command(ContributedCommand { id, title, keybinding }).build()?`; validation rejects empty/padded/control-character/overly long/non-portable IDs, names, versions, entry points, duplicate command/panel IDs, menu items referencing missing commands, and non-object settings schemas; `runtime.load(manifest)?`; `runtime.activate_with_broker(&id, &PermissionBroker::new())?`; `runtime.broadcast_notification(ExtensionNotification::SettingsChanged { key, value })`; inspect `PluginManifest::to_text()`, `Contributions::to_text()`, contribution `to_text()` helpers, `ExtensionInfo::to_text()`, `ExtensionHost::to_text()`, `ExtensionManifest::to_text()`, `ExtensionDiagnostics::to_text()`, `ExtensionRegistry::to_text()`, and command catalog `PaletteCommandId`/`CommandDescriptor`/`CommandPalette::to_text()` without logging extension IDs, names, entry paths, command IDs, labels, keybindings, authors, activation events, errors, or icons.

## Theming

One pipeline, two cooperating types: `kael::Theme` is the serializable, file-facing theme (`colors`/`typography`/`spacing`/`radii`/`shadows`) the hot-reload watcher reloads; `kael_ui::Theme` (`variant` + rich `ThemeTokens`) is the runtime token system components render from. Flow: `theme.toml` → `kael::Theme` (Global) → `ThemeTokens` (bridge) → components.

```rust
kael_ui::init(cx);
install_theme(cx, Theme::dark()); // 18 presets, or Theme::custom(ThemeTokens { ..ThemeTokens::dark() })
install_theme_file_bridge(cx); // maps reloaded kael::Theme -> ThemeTokens, then install_theme
cx.observe_theme_file("theme.toml", |theme, cx| cx.set_global(theme))?; // file → kael::Theme → bridge → live restyle
let theme = Theme::of(cx); // read tokens: theme.tokens.background, theme.tokens.primary, ...
```

Custom mapping: register your own `cx.observe_theme_files(|core, cx| ...)` subscriber, optionally via `tokens_from_core_theme(core, base)`.

## Event pattern

All callbacks: `|data, &mut Window, &mut App/Context| { entity.update(cx, |this, cx| { this.mutate(); cx.notify(); }); }`

## Platform support

macOS (Metal), Windows (DirectX 11), Linux X11/Wayland (Vulkan/Blade)
